belief: The world is getting worse and worse.
origins: News thrives on alarm, and a steady feed of tragedy gives the impression that everything is collapsing. Older generations may say, “It was better in my day.” Anxiety rises and joy and hope fade.
teaches: Solomon wrote, “What has been will be again, and what has been done will be done again; there is nothing new under the sun,” and cautioned that it is unwise to ask why the old days were better than these (Ecclesiastes 7:10). Jesus said, “In the world you will have tribulation. But take courage; I have overcome the world!” Paul wrote that “in the last days terrible times will come,” so Christians are not surprised by trouble. But we are called to live with courage and hope, trusting God, who holds everything together.
errors: Seeing the world as only getting worse.
Feeling alarmed and concluding that it must be catastrophic.
questions: What news sources am I taking in, and how often?
What good is happening that I do not hear about?
What did people in earlier generations face?
What does Jesus promise in a troubled world?
What helps me stay informed without being overwhelmed?
What good can I do near me?
truth: Trouble is real, but Jesus has overcome the world. I can stay informed in moderation, notice what is good, and hold onto hope and courage.
hw_truths: I can limit what I take in.
log: Each week, note three good things you noticed.
actions: Write three good things each day.
Say it when you feel alarmed.
prayer: Lord, the news weighs on me. Thank You that You have overcome the world. Give me courage, hope, and a heart to do good where I am. Amen.
hw_questions: What news do I take in?
How can I stay informed calmly?
name_example: Sarah can write: “Jesus has overcome the world, so I can take courage.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “The world is getting worse and worse.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
